exposure: age of pregnancy (35 years and older vs. 30-34 years)
cohort: Pregnant women who gave birth in Vakif Gureba Training and Research Hospital, Clinic of Obstetrics and Gynecology in 2006
finding: There were no significant differences in pregnancy outcomes between pregnant women aged 35 years and older compared to those aged 30-34 years.
mod_finding: The most common cause of cesarean section indication was fetal distress in the advanced maternal age group, whereas previous cesarean section was the most common cause in the younger group.
